newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Russia's Yeltsin ends visit to Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Yeltsin ends visit to Ukraine.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin ended his first official visit to Ukraine on Saturday after signing a wide-ranging friendship treaty with the Ukrainian leader Leonid Kuchma.
President Kuchma, who broke protocol to personally see Yeltsin off at Kiev's Boryspil airport, said he was strongly impressed by the results of the summit.
"This was an event of huge importance which opens a new stage in relations between our two countries," Kuchma told reporters after Yeltsin's departure.
Kuchma made clear that he hoped the new friendship treaty with Russia would help harmonise relations between the two former Soviet republics and make them more equal.
"Ukraine is a smaller country than Russia but there are fewer politicians in Russia now who think that Ukraine can be strangled by force and kept as a vassal," he said.
Earlier on Saturday the two leaders signed the friendship treaty and a broad political declaration outlining their common approaches to some bilateral and international issues.
They also signed a document hailing the deal on the disputed Black Sea fleet reached by Kuchma and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Wednesday and a declaration on space cooperation.

The deal on the fleet, under which Russia won a 20-year lease of the Crimean port of Sevastopol to base its share of the former Soviet naval force, has solved the most painful problem which had soured relations between Moscow and Kiev.
Chernomyrdin and Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko have also agreed to remove obstacles to bilateral trade.
"We have been losing $10 billion each year because of what amounts to an economic war," Kuchma said, praising progress in trade talks.
